v1.feedback: Strong execution of 'rebound' via physics-driven face morphing through genealogical states with collision feedback. The restrained earth-tone palette and readable facial point-cloud silhouette align well with taste. Minor improvements: reduce the jitter amplitude during transitions (currently 0.08 feels visually noisy), and consider tightening the collision sphere radius to increase rebound frequency — the 6-unit wall creates long drift periods where the concept isn't active. The squash-stretch on impact is elegant but could be more pronounced (currently 0.3/0.5 coefficients are subtle at distance).

v2.feedback: The piece executes 'rebound' literally and cleverly: a bouncing point cloud that morphs through three procedurally-generated face geometries with squash-stretch physics. The face silhouettes are recognizable (forehead/eyes/nose/jaw structure reads clearly), palette is restrained warm monochrome, and the genealogical cycling concept lands. Two refinements: the jitter animation during morph transitions feels slightly muddy—consider reducing it further or making it directional along morph flow rather than omni-axis noise; the squash-stretch could be more pronounced or asymmetric to emphasize impact direction (current 0.2/0.7 range is decent but could push to 0.15/0.85 for real cartoon physics).
